# KDF reference vectors

These are fixed expected values, not values generated by the Go implementation.

- Two AES-128 session-key vectors are the ECDH worked example from OpenPACE
  src/eactest.c: tc_ecdh_shared_secret_k, tc_ecdh_k_enc, tc_ecdh_k_mac.
  The upstream comment attributes them to BSI's EAC Worked Example v1.01.
- Eighteen additional synthetic vectors cover AES-128/192/256, purpose counters
  1/2/3, and both absent and nonempty nonce. They were calculated independently
  with Python hashlib and verified with the OpenSSL command-line digest tool.
  They are not claimed to be published BSI test vectors.

Pinned upstream revision: 40a5181b6abff751f756be980bfa165eb02677be.

Sources:
- https://github.com/frankmorgner/openpace/blob/40a5181b6abff751f756be980bfa165eb02677be/src/eactest.c
- https://github.com/frankmorgner/openpace/blob/40a5181b6abff751f756be980bfa165eb02677be/src/eac_kdf.c
- https://github.com/frankmorgner/openpace/blob/40a5181b6abff751f756be980bfa165eb02677be/src/eac_lib.c

The input is secret || optional nonce || purpose (four-byte big-endian).
AES-128 uses SHA-1, AES-192/256 use SHA-256. Truncate one digest to the AES
key size; do not expand by incrementing purpose. SHA-1 here is a mandatory
protocol KDF operation, not a signature algorithm.

Run python kdf/testdata/verify.py with Python 3 and OpenSSL on PATH.
It verifies the fixtures without importing or executing any Go code and never
rewrites them. Normal go test ./... needs neither Python nor OpenSSL.
